Summary:
Quick culture-fit / screening call for Senior SRE candidate. Focus on background, on-call experience, incident handling, infra preferences (cloud vs on-prem), and naive fit with Redwood's inference platform. Candidate currently at NimbleStack, interested in production-first infra focused role.
Topics: background, on-call cadence, incident postmortem, infra infra choices (k8s, autoscaling), security/compliance comfort, notice period, compensation expectations.
---
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey Olivia, thanks for joining — I'm Lena from Talent, Marcus is our hiring manager, he'll intro the role. Quick heads up recording is on.
[00:18] Olivia Reyes: Hi yeah thanks, excited to chat. Morning, Marcus.
[00:22] Marcus Li: Hi Olivia, quick intro — I'm Marcus, I run infra at Redwood Inference. We're building a serving runtime for LLMs, focusing on latency and reliability at scale. Today is mostly a cultural/ops fit, a little technical questions but not a heavy algo interview.
[00:40] Olivia Reyes: Sounds great, happy to go through my background.
[00:45] Lena Ortiz: We'll do 30-ish minutes, and then if both sides feel good we'll schedule the deeper technical loop.
[00:53] Marcus Li: Cool. Olivia, can you give a quick 3-minute summary of your last two roles and on-call responsibilities?
[01:03] Olivia Reyes: Sure. For the past three years I was Senior SRE at NimbleStack — we run a distributed data ingest pipeline and real-time feature store. I was on a four-week rotation with one week primary pager, one week secondary, others were follow. I did incident lead for sev-1s, root cause work, and I helped build our autoscaling controller. Prior to that I was at ClearScale where I focused on cloud migrations and infra-as-code. I also own runbooks and postmortems.
[01:39] Marcus Li: When you say autoscaling controller, is that HPA-based or something custom?
[01:45] Olivia Reyes: It's somewhat custom — we extended the k8s HPA with a custom controller to include throughput signals and queue depth. We also had a cheap KV cache for prefix results — "KV cash" sometimes in the logs — so sorry for the typo in my notes — but we used that to short-circuit some requests during spikes.
[02:12] Marcus Li: Nice. At Redwood we also use custom routing and cache layers for inference; curious how you handled cold-start latency and cache invalidation.
[02:24] Olivia Reyes: We observed model warm-up similar to what you'd expect — we used a combination of predictive warm-up and keeping a small pool of pre-warmed pods for the common path. For invalidation, we drained keys based on TTL and used a versioned prefix so we could do bulk invalidation during deploys. There were occasional race conditions, yes.
[02:48] Lena Ortiz: (laughs) race conditions are a feature right?
[02:52] Olivia Reyes: They keep you humble.
[02:54] [03:00] Marcus Li: Can you walk through an incident you led recently, the timeline, and what changed after?
[03:07] Olivia Reyes: Yeah — two months ago we had a sev-1 where an upstream schema change produced a malformed record that blew up ingestion workers. The timeline was: 03:15 alerted by synthetic checks, 03:20 paged primary on-call, 03:35 we deduced parser exception, 03:50 rolled back the schema change and throttled producers. I took lead for communications to customers. Postmortem found lack of schema contract testing in CI; we introduced a gating job and a compensating consumer for schema validation, also added a canary deployment step.
[03:47] Marcus Li: Did you do any tabletop exercises or simulate the failure after or before the fix?
[03:54] Olivia Reyes: We did a tabletop within a week and a small chaos experiment to confirm fallback paths. We also improved runbook clarity; there was some confusion on restoring the consumer backlog.
[04:09] [04:15] Marcus Li: Good. How comfortable are you with hardware level issues — GPUs, NVMe, kernel tuning — given that we have GPU-based inference nodes?
[04:24] Olivia Reyes: I've not managed large GPU farms in production but I've done infra for GPU-enabled ML infra at ClearScale for a proof-of-concept: NVMe sizing, driver upgrades, and eviction behavior under memory pressure. I'm comfortable reading metrics, coordinating with ML engineers, and building runbooks. I'd be eager to deepen OS/kernel level debugging.
[04:50] Marcus Li: That's reasonable. We don't expect everyone to be a kernel dev; more important is that you can triage, escalate, and own the mitigation.
[05:00] [05:05] Lena Ortiz: Do you have a preference for remote/on-site? We are primarily remote but we have quarterly collab weeks in SF.
[05:12] Olivia Reyes: I'm remote-first, but I can travel quarterly. Fair.
[05:18] [05:24] Marcus Li: What's your notice period and comp target?
[05:28] Olivia Reyes: I have a standard 4-week notice. Comp target is in the 200-240k range total comp depending on equity, benefits, and team.
[05:41] Marcus Li: Thanks. Back to ops — what's your experience with chaos engineering or load testing for bursty workloads?
[05:49] Olivia Reyes: We used locust for load tests and a custom traffic-replay job. For chaos, we ran pod-terminate and DNS delay experiments. For bursty workloads we tuned request queuing and set different MES (service-level) profiles — some of this was ad-hoc due to time constraints.
[06:17] [06:22] Marcus Li: So you'd be comfortable building a load plan for a new model rollout?
[06:26] Olivia Reyes: Yes, I can scope RPS targets, SLOs, and propose canary percentage ramps.
[06:32] [06:37] Lena Ortiz: What attracts you to Redwood?
[06:40] Olivia Reyes: I'm excited by the inference domain — the perf tradeoffs and reliability constraints are interesting. Also the focus on developer experience and tooling sounds like a place I could have impact.
[06:52] Marcus Li: Great. Any concerns or missing skills you think we should know about?
[06:58] Olivia Reyes: Just the GPU ops bit — otherwise fairly confident. I wanted to ask about career progression for SREs here and cross-team exposure.
[07:08] Marcus Li: We usually rotate people through platform and model infra; we support goal paths to tech lead or manager if that's desired.
[07:18] [07:25] Marcus Li: Quick technical check — how comfortable are you with Kubernetes API server debugging? Eg apiserver audit logs, etcd compaction issues, and control-plane observation?
[07:34] Olivia Reyes: Comfortable — we've debugged etcd quorum splits, compaction backlogs; used etcdctl snapshot/restore during a recovery and improved monitoring to alert on WAL growth. I've written small operators but not large scale controllers.
[07:52] Marcus Li: Good. We sometimes hit subtle problems in autoscaler interactions and the kubelet eviction logic.
[07:58] Olivia Reyes: Yeah that's always fun.
[08:01] [08:05] Lena Ortiz: A quick logistical question: are there any constraints on your start date or compensation discussions?
[08:10] Olivia Reyes: Start date depends on negotiation; earliest would be early September after notice + wrap-up. Compensation open to discuss.
[08:20] Marcus Li: Ok. We'll probably aim for a tech deep dive next — 2-3 interviews, include a postmortem walkthrough and a systems design focused on scale and latency.
[08:32] Olivia Reyes: That sounds aligned.
[08:35] [08:40] Marcus Li: One more operational question — how have you handled secrets and KMS rotation in previous roles?
[08:47] Olivia Reyes: We used a centralized KMS (cloud provider KMS) with nightly rotation and a secrets operator to inject into k8s. For on-prem we used HashiCorp Vault with TLS-auth and periodic token bridging. We also tightly controlled service accounts and used ephemeral credentials for CI.
[09:09] Marcus Li: Good. Our Private customers sometimes require HSM integrations, so experience with Vault is a plus.
[09:17] Olivia Reyes: I've managed Vault in production for a while.
[09:20] [09:24] Lena Ortiz: Anything else you'd like to ask us?
[09:28] Olivia Reyes: How big is the SRE org and tooling expectations for new hires?
[09:33] Marcus Li: Small team today — maybe 8 engineers in infra across services and platform. New hires often own a critical path such as observability or scaling. We expect people to be pragmatic with tooling, ship automation, and write runbooks.
[09:48] Olivia Reyes: Cool.
[09:50] [09:55] Marcus Li: Do you have a link or artifact showing a postmortem or runbook? You mentioned sharing a sample.
[09:59] Olivia Reyes: I have a sanitized postmortem in a public gist, I'll share after the call.
[10:05] [10:10] Lena Ortiz: Great, please reply to the calendar invite with that link.
[10:13] Olivia Reyes: Will do.
[10:15] [10:20] Marcus Li: Any allergies to pager timing? We do rotating nights ~1 week every two months but we try to be mindful.
[10:28] Olivia Reyes: That schedule works for me. I've done on-call for years.
[10:32] [10:36] Lena Ortiz: Wrap-up: both sides seem positive. We'll send loop details and aim to schedule the tech loop next week.
[10:44] Marcus Li: Final note — are you comfortable with redaction and NDA processes? For some private deployments we sign NDAs and require a short background check.
[10:53] Olivia Reyes: Yes, I can complete standard checks. NDA's fine.
[10:58] [11:02] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, Olivia. We'll follow up with next steps.
[11:06] Olivia Reyes: Thanks everyone, appreciate the time.
